clue.text: Bake ground British meat served on skewer

indicators.note: something ground is crushed and broken up, so the word before it is reworked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as fodder
B is the standard abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A recipe step: bake some minced British meat and serve it on a skewer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like a description of the meat, as in mince, but it tells you to rearrange the letters of Bake.
explanation.definitionFit: A kebab is pieces of meat cooked and served threaded on a skewer, so the phrase describes the dish.

clue.text: Learner donning Christopher's traditional garment

indicators.note: donning means putting on clothes, so one piece is wrapped inside another like a body in a garment

parts.note: Kit is a short form of the name Christopher
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A learner driver dresses up in Christopher's national costume.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside KIT to make KILT. Kit is a familiar short form of Christopher, as in the playwright Kit Marlowe.
explanation.definitionFit: The kilt is the pleated tartan skirt worn as Scottish national dress, a classic example of traditional clothing.

clue.text: Singer, born idiot

parts.note: b. is the abbreviation for born in biographies
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: An insult: this singer was simply born stupid.
explanation.definitionFit: A bass is a male singer with the lowest vocal range, so the word names a kind of singer.

clue.text: Cricketer on the drink in London district

parts.note: a batter is the cricketer who bats
'the drink' is slang for the sea
in a down clue, one piece 'on' another sits above it, so the cricketer comes first

explanation.surface: A cricketer has been drinking in a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the drink' sounds like a drinking spree, but 'the drink' is the sea, as in falling in the drink. BATTERSEA is a district of south-west London on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: Battersea is a well-known area of south London, home to the power station and dogs' home.

clue.text: Dramatic moans voiced with microphone

indicators.note: voiced means spoken out, so the word is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: sighs are moans; said out loud they match the first syllables
mic is the usual short form of microphone

explanation.surface: Someone makes a big show of groaning into a microphone.
explanation.definitionFit: Seismic, literally about earthquakes, is used figuratively for something huge and dramatic, like a seismic shift.

clue.text: Boy having to collect trophy? Precisely correct

indicators.note: to collect something is to gather it in, so one word takes the other inside it

parts.note: a son is a boy
pot is sporting slang for a cup or trophy

explanation.surface: A boy must go and pick up a trophy he has won.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the slangy use of pot for a sporting cup, as in winning some pots.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot on is an informal British idiom meaning exactly right or accurate.

clue.text: Island politician a little devil

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for island
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An island's politician is described as something of a rascal.
explanation.definitionFit: An imp is a small mischievous sprite or demon, so it is a minor devil.

clue.text: Get Margo prepared for an expensive commitment?

indicators.note: to prepare something is to make it ready by working it into shape, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Is Margo ready to take on a costly obligation?
explanation.definitionFit: A mortgage is a long-term home loan, typically the largest financial obligation a household takes on.

clue.text: Something painful insensitive lover boy raised

parts.note: a cold person is unfeeling

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word lifts it from bottom to top, so it is read upwards

parts.note: Eros is the Greek boy-god of love

explanation.surface: A heartless boyfriend brought up a painful subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold sore is a sore blister near the mouth caused by a virus, so it is a painful thing.

clue.text: Carlyle so thought to contain kingdom

indicators.note: the run of words holds the answer within itself, spanning their joins

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, all of the second, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: The historian Thomas Carlyle supposedly believed something should include a kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesotho is a mountainous kingdom in southern Africa, entirely surrounded by South Africa.

clue.text: Danger for each one left

parts.note: per means for each, as in per head
I is the Roman numeral one
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A risk applies to every single person who remains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For each' looks like one unit meaning per; here 'for' is the link and 'each' alone gives PER.
explanation.definitionFit: Peril is serious risk or danger, a near synonym used in phrases like in mortal peril.

clue.text: Riotous House as GOP reveals food delivery route

indicators.note: riotous means wild and disorderly, so the letters that follow are thrown out of order

parts.note: the ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An unruly House of Representatives exposes something about the Republicans.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is US politics: the House is Congress's lower chamber and the GOP is the Republican Party.
explanation.definitionFit: The oesophagus is the gullet, the tube that carries swallowed food from the throat to the stomach.

clue.text: A single drop of the hard stuff?

definitions.text: A single drop of the hard stuff?

parts.words: A single drop of the hard stuff?
parts.note: surface reading: one measure of strong spirits, a single nip of whisky

parts.words: A single drop of the hard stuff?
parts.note: setter's reading: one falling piece of frozen precipitation, which is literally hard

explanation.surface: A drinker asks for just one shot of strong liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The hard stuff' is slang for spirits, but here it means solid ice falling from the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Hail falls as hard ice pellets, and each individual pellet is one drop of this hard precipitation.

clue.text: Ginger beer right for crisis situation

parts.note: ginger hair is red
ale is a type of beer
RT is an abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Ginger beer is the right drink when things go badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ginger beer' reads as one drink, but splits into a colour and a beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Red alert is the highest state of readiness, declared when an emergency or crisis is imminent.

clue.text: Saw old king in horrible mishap

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the jumbled word
something horrible is a mess, so the letters of the following word are jumbled

parts.note: fodder to rearrange
O is an abbreviation for old
R is for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone witnessed an aged monarch in a terrible accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past tense of see, but it is the noun meaning a saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old proverb or maxim, and an aphorism is a pithy statement of a general truth.

clue.text: Former model in show

parts.note: ex- means former
to model is to pose for an artist or photographer

explanation.surface: An ex-model appears in a fashion show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' and 'show' suggest nouns from the catwalk; both act as verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: To expose something is to reveal or display it, so it can stand for the verb show.

clue.text: Campanologist's double?

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as asking for a bell-ringer's lookalike; the two halves are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: One who rings bells is literally a ringer, and a person closely resembling another is called a ringer.

clue.text: Private investigator in unruly Mayo seeing problem

indicators.note: in places the detective inside the scrambled letters
unruly means out of control, so the letters of the county are scrambled

parts.note: fodder to rearrange
PI is the abbreviation for private investigator

explanation.surface: A private detective in rowdy County Mayo, Ireland, has trouble with his eyesight.
explanation.definitionFit: Myopia is short-sightedness, a defect of vision in which distant objects look blurred.

clue.text: Short ballad penned by a writer in World's End

indicators.note: something penned by another is held inside it, as if written in an enclosure

parts.note: taken as written
Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a calypso is a Caribbean ballad-style song

explanation.surface: A writer works a brief ballad into a story set at the end of the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'World's End' looks like a place name (it is a London pub area), but it simply means the end of the world.
explanation.definitionFit: The apocalypse is the prophesied destruction of the world, its final catastrophic ending.

clue.text: Moved suddenly — photograph ruined

definitions.meaning: third meaning: worn out or broken

explanation.walkthrough: Three separate meanings of one word sit side by side; the surface suggests someone jogged a camera and spoilt a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the past of the verb for darting, a noun for a snapshot, and slang for wrecked.

clue.text: Energy worker climbing fiery mountain

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means going upward, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: An energetic labourer scales a volcano.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is the active volcano on Sicily, so it is a mountain that erupts with fire.

clue.text: Direction and distance leading to Zola?

parts.note: E for east, a compass direction
a mile is a unit of distance

explanation.surface: A route-finder giving the way and distance to someone called Zola.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading to Zola' sounds like route directions, but it means the name that comes before Zola.
explanation.definitionFit: The French novelist was Émile Zola, so this forename precedes his surname.

clue.text: Swelled head? Say nothing!

parts.note: e.g. means for example, as does say
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone is told: if you are big-headed, keep quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Ego is self-esteem; an inflated one is what we call a swelled head, so the question mark marks it as loose.

clue.text: Forecaster to gain advantage we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is taken by its spoken sound, not spelling

parts.note: to profit is to gain an advantage

explanation.surface: A forecaster uses predictions to get ahead, it is said.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophet foretells the future, so he is someone who forecasts what will happen.

clue.text: Drum roll to precede result in this lottery?

definitions.text: Drum roll to precede result in this lottery?

parts.words: Drum roll to precede result in this lottery?
parts.note: surface reading: a drummer's roll builds suspense before a draw is announced

parts.words: Drum roll to precede result in this lottery?
parts.note: setter's reading: a revolving drum is literally rolled round to mix tickets before the winning one is pulled out

explanation.surface: A dramatic drum roll before the winner of a draw is revealed.
explanation.walkthrough: The drum roll is not percussion: the tickets sit in a turning drum that is spun before a draw.
explanation.definitionFit: A tombola is a raffle at fêtes where tickets are drawn from a rotating drum.

clue.text: Exceptionally wide for instance

definitions.meaning: second meaning: in cricket, a wide is a run given to the batting side without the ball being hit

explanation.walkthrough: 'Exceptionally wide' reads as one phrase meaning very broad; split it. In cricket a wide is a ball bowled out of the batter's reach, scoring a bonus run.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means especially, and in cricket wides, byes and no-balls are runs not hit off the bat.
